title: He gave a promise.
paragraphs:
Not because God forgot Abraham.
Because faith that is real is usually forged in delay.

God told Abraham he would become the father of many nations.
But the promise did not arrive in a week.
Or a year.
It took decades.
And that kind of waiting can expose everything.

The fear.
The doubt.
The temptation to “help God out” with fleshly shortcuts.
The ache of holding a word from heaven while your hands stay empty on earth.
But here’s what we miss: God was not only preparing Isaac.

Because a delayed promise is not always a denied promise. Scripture says, “And after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise” (Hebrews 6:15). And Romans 4 shows us Abraham’s faith grew strong as he gave glory to God, fully convinced that what God had promised, God was able to perform.
That is the Gospel rhythm too.

God made a promise.
Humanity waited.
Generations passed.
Then Christ came.

Jesus is proof that God does not break covenant.
Not one word falls to the ground.
If you are in a season where heaven feels slow, do not confuse delay with abandonment.
The God who kept His word to Abraham has kept His word in Christ—and because of Jesus, your waiting is never wasted.

Hold on.
The story is not over.
